title: Customer-fidelity load generator for Private/VPC reproductions
creator: Priya Singh
description: Build a reproducible, configurable load generator that can emulate customer traffic and environment characteristics for Private/VPC/on-prem Redwood deployments. The harness must produce stable, repeatable tokens/sec profiles and p95 latency distributions so we can attribute regressions to runtime/kernel/scheduling changes rather than test noise. Key features: replay of snapped request traces, synthetic traffic distributions (session lengths, user think-time, prompt prefixes), KV-cache warmup profiles, N-to-1 routing for multi-tenant simulations, network condition emulation (bandwidth, latency, jitter), and an automated regression detector that compares current runs to baseline runs and opens a ticket when drift exceeds thresholds. Outputs must integrate with Prometheus/Grafana and Redwood Console dashboards (token/sec, p95, p99, error-rate, cost-per-token).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay a stored customer snapshot and reproduce tokens/sec within +/- 7% for stable workloads
End-to-end runs capture p50/p95/p99 and have <5% run-to-run variance on synthetic workloads
Automated regression detector flags a run when tokens/sec or p95 deviates from baseline beyond configured thresholds and creates ENG ticket with attached artifacts
Outputs exported to Prometheus metrics and a Grafana dashboard template; Console ingestion endpoint documented
Runbook and onboarding doc created for Solutions/SEs describing how to create a snapshot and execute a reproduce run
steps: Design snapshot format: requests, auth tokens metadata, kv-cache warmup sequences, sequence-length histogram
Prototype replay engine in Go (reuse runtime client and batching hooks) and a lightweight Python runner for scenario templates
Add network/emulation layer using tc/netem container wrapper for latency/bandwidth jitter
Wire Prometheus exporter and Grafana dashboard; add Console ingestion events and tracing hooks
Implement regression detector using windowed comparison and bootstrapped thresholds; wire to alerting and auto-ticket creation
Validate against three customer snapshots and two internal synthetic scenarios; measure variance and tune seeding/warmups
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting - aligned on snapshot schema and core metrics (tokens/sec, p95, error_rate). Decided to prioritize reproducibility over max throughput for initial phase.

2026-02-27: Prototype replay engine skeleton completed (Go). Basic request pacing and KV-cache warmup implemented. Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/repro-load-gen PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-load-gen/pull/12

2026-03-02: Ran first end-to-end runs against private-staging cluster. Observed high variance for p95 on bursty chat workloads; traced to missing prefix-caching step. Added KV cache priming in replay sequence.

2026-03-05: Design review with Runtime team. Runtime requested option to toggle kernel scheduling hints and batch window to help isolate regressions. Agreed to add scheduling flags and document compatibility.

2026-03-09: Regression detector MVP implemented. Configurable thresholds (absolute and percentage) and bootstrap baseline capture. Hooked to ticket creation workflow: creates ENG ticket with run artifacts (S3 link) when triggered.

2026-03-10: QA runs against two customer snapshots completed. Tokens/sec within target for steady workloads; p95 variance reduced to ~6% after cache priming and adding network emulation. Follow-up: improve trace anonymization and harden auth replay for VPC customers.
decisions: Use request-level snapshot format rather than full VM images to keep storage and replay lightweight
Implement replay core in Go for low-latency control loops; scenario templating in Python for convenience
Expose kernel scheduling and batching hints as runtime flags to help isolate performance regressions
Regression detector will use a two-layer threshold: absolute floor (e.g., p95 > 500ms) and relative delta vs baseline (e.g., >12%)
blockers: Need Secure Vault access for pulling redacted customer auth tokens for replay in staging — security ticket raised
Some customer snapshots include proprietary attachments not yet supported by our replay schema; Solutions engineering to provide sanitized samples
Grafana dashboard template blocked by infra team change to metrics namespace mapping (awaiting infra-ops approval)
monitoring_metrics: run_to_run_variance (stddev of p95 across N runs)
notes: Next: unblock Vault access with Security; plan a data-sanitization pass with Solutions by 2026-03-18
Schedule a cross-team demo for Runtime and Console on 2026-03-22 to validate metrics ingestion
Longer-term: integrate with CI to run lightweight reproducibility checks on every runtime release candidate
